19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容

### 5.3 用词黑名单

- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写

---

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Test-time compute scaling has emerged as a complement to model scaling \cite{snell2025scaling}: repeated sampling with majority voting \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}, best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, brown2024monkeys}, and extended chain-of-thought \cite{muennighoff2025s1} yield large gains on reasoning and code generation, but the evidence concentrates on tasks with discrete answers or execution-based verification.
Named entity recognition (NER) poses a structurally different challenge: the output is a \textit{set} of entities, two samples may extract overlapping but non-identical sets, and there is no obvious majority to vote on.
This challenge generalizes to any \textit{set-valued} structured prediction task where outputs admit partial but not exact overlap.

Prior work on confidence estimation for LLM-based IE has conflated \textit{quality estimation} (which inputs does the model handle reliably?) with \textit{sample selection} (which of $N$ outputs is best?).
Existing self-consistency methods \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, chen2024usc, taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty} assume outputs can be grouped by equivalence, an assumption that breaks for entity sets with partial overlap.
Unlike \citet{yao2026consistency}, who demonstrate that self-consistency correlates with task accuracy, we provide the first systematic empirical characterization of \textit{when and why} test-time scaling via LP-based selection succeeds or fails for structured prediction, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as the two blocking mechanisms.

A key distinction structures our analysis: four of five signals (Soft Jaccard, voting confidence, Fleiss' $\kappa$, exact match) are instance-level aggregates that assign identical scores to all $N$ candidates for a given input; only log-probability (LP) is natively per-sample.
All signals achieve reliable quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82; Figure~\ref{fig:overview}), supporting selective prediction.
For selection, LP achieves $+1.39$~pp on Few-NERD ($p{<}0.001$) in settings where both low instance degeneracy and adequate alignment are present, with gains scaling with $N$.
On SciERC, the observed LP gain ($+0.2$~pp, $p{=}0.29$) falls below the minimum detectable effect (${\approx}$1.5~pp at 80\% power, $n{=}529$) despite 13~pp oracle headroom. We term this disparity between quality estimation strength and selection effectiveness the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}.
Three factors qualitatively shape this gap: (a)~\textit{instance degeneracy} (13\textendash 68\% across our benchmarks) compresses the candidate space; (b)~\textit{oracle headroom} bounds the achievable gain; (c)~\textit{LP-quality alignment} (within-instance $\rho(\text{LP}, \text{F1})$) determines whether LP can discriminate candidates in non-degenerate instances (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
Our diagnosis complements MBR utility misalignment \cite{eikema2025structured}: degeneracy eliminates candidate diversity before utility alignment matters (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Both mechanisms intensify with model capability: degeneracy rises with training convergence and varies across model families rather than scaling monotonically with parameter count (\S\ref{sec:scaling}). This creates a tension between model quality and test-time improvability.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_overview}
\caption{Overview of the correlation-selection gap. \textbf{Left}: consistency signals estimate instance quality ($\rho$ up to 0.45; Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}). \textbf{Center}: instance-level signals assign identical scores to all $N$ candidates, so selection cannot outperform greedy. \textbf{Right}: entity-level construction via majority vote ($\theta{=}2/N$) bypasses the bottleneck ($+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD; \S\ref{sec:prescriptive}).}
\label{fig:overview}
\end{figure*}

We evaluate five signals on four NER benchmarks (SciERC \cite{luan2018scierc}, Few-NERD \cite{ding2021fewnerd}, CoNLL-2003 \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll}, WNUT-17 \cite{derczynski2017wnut}) spanning a difficulty gradient, using two 8B models (Qwen3-8B, LLaMA-3.1-8B) with a 4B ablation, varying $N{\in}\{2,\ldots,32\}$ and model capacity across 4B\textendash 8B fine-tuned and 72B zero-shot regimes.
Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Quality estimation as a test-time scaling diagnostic.}
    Five signals from three families evaluated on four NER benchmarks, two model families, and a 4B ablation, achieving reliable quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82).
    QE enables selective prediction: filtering low-confidence instances at 80\% coverage yields $+5$--$8$\,pp F1 (AUPRC 0.70--0.92, VC strongest; \S\ref{sec:prescriptive}).

    \item \textbf{Failure modes of test-time scaling for structured prediction.}
    For fine-tuned 4B--8B models, LP-quality alignment (within-instance $\rho(\text{LP}, \text{F1})$) is the primary predictor of selection success: LP achieves $+1.39$~pp on Few-NERD ($p{<}0.001$) where alignment is strong, but not on benchmarks with weak alignment.
    Instance degeneracy causally modulates LP within fixed settings (epoch and temperature ablations) but does not predict cross-dataset direction ($\rho{=}0.052$, 23 configurations); supervised combinations and hidden state probes (Appendix~\ref{app:hidden_probe}) confirm the gap persists.
    The resulting three-step diagnostic (measure degeneracy, assess signal alignment, choose aggregation) provides a reusable protocol for structured test-time scaling (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

    \item \textbf{Entity-level construction as a partial mitigation for structured test-time scaling failures.}
    The diagnostic naturally motivates entity-level aggregation, adapting entity voting from ensemble NER \cite{florian2003named} to stochastic sampling: under fine-tuning and zero-shot regimes, LP-weighted construction yields $+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD and $+1.02$\,pp on SciERC (multi-seed mean, $p{<}0.005$; \S\ref{sec:prescriptive}).
    Construction and LP selection are complementary, governed by LP-quality alignment.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

Effective selection likely requires content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, venktesh2025trust}.
Three factors constrain selection: degeneracy (17.8--67.9\%), limited headroom, and LP-quality alignment ($\rho$ 0.043--0.667); within non-degenerate instances, MBR utility correlates with F1 ($\rho{=}0.524$) \cite{eikema2022sampling}.
Where LP compression is mitigated (range ${\geq}0.05$, $n{=}210$), LP yields $+2.9$~pp ($p{=}0.004$; Table~\ref{tab:nontied_main}), though $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ is post-hoc ($p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.14$; Appendix~\ref{app:epsilon_robustness}).
Temperature disentangles degeneracy from alignment: at $T{=}1.2$, degeneracy drops to 14.9\% yet LP does not improve ($\rho{=}0.225$; Table~\ref{tab:t_degeneracy}); the selection window narrows with model improvement \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, snell2025scaling}.

\paragraph{From diagnosis to practice.}\label{sec:selection_method}
Entity-level construction bypasses both failure mechanisms (Table~\ref{tab:entity_construction}). Degeneracy gates effectiveness: across seven conditions (two model families, two prompting regimes, three datasets), gains are positive when degeneracy ${<}22$\% and absent when ${>}31$\% (all $p{<}0.01$; epoch ablations confirm within-dataset, Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}). Under 72B few-shot, construction fails despite low degeneracy, indicating that demonstrations alter diversity structure beyond simple error correlation (Appendix~\ref{app:fs_error}). QE signals remain effective under few-shot (SJ $\rho$ 0.29--0.44), confirming that quality estimation is regime-independent even when construction is not.
Alternative strategies (DALS, MBR, DGS) fail to beat greedy (Appendix~\ref{app:dals}); these negative results are specific to fine-tuned models with constrained decoding (Appendix~\ref{app:when_selection_works}).

I found the research paper you were looking for. The arXiv paper 2503.15850 is titled "Uncertainty Quantification and Confidence Calibration in Large Language Models: A Survey" by Xiaoou Liu and colleagues.

Here are the key details about the paper:

**Main Focus:**
The paper addresses how Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in text generation, reasoning, and decision-making, but their reliability is a major concern as they often produce plausible but incorrect responses. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) enhances trustworthiness by estimating confidence in outputs, enabling risk mitigation and selective prediction.

**Key Challenges:**
Traditional UQ methods struggle with LLMs due to computational constraints and decoding inconsistencies. Moreover, LLMs introduce unique uncertainty sources, such as input ambiguity, reasoning path divergence, and decoding stochasticity, that extend beyond classical aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.

**Approach:**
The paper introduces a new taxonomy that categorizes UQ methods based on computational efficiency and uncertainty dimensions (input, reasoning, parameter, and prediction uncertainty).

**Conformal Prediction:**
Conformal Prediction (CP) is a statistical framework that provides formal coverage guarantees for uncertainty estimation in LLMs.

The paper was submitted on March 20, 2025, with a revised version as of June 3, 2025.

\begin{abstract}
Test-time compute scaling---repeated sampling with selection or aggregation---yields large gains on discrete-answer reasoning and code generation, but named entity recognition (NER) produces \textit{sets} of entities with partial overlap, where standard aggregation mechanisms break down.
We evaluate five confidence signals for quality estimation (QE) and sample selection on four NER benchmarks across fine-tuned 4B\textendash 8B and zero-shot 72B models.
All signals achieve reliable QE ($\rho$ up to 0.45 on CoNLL-2003, area under the ROC curve [AUROC] up to 0.82), enabling selective prediction ($+5$--$8$\,pp F1 at 80\% coverage).
For instance-level selection, log-probability (LP) succeeds only where LP-quality alignment is strong, and gains are absent elsewhere despite large oracle headroom (the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}).
We diagnose three structural failure modes---instance degeneracy, limited oracle headroom, and LP compression---that persist at 72B zero-shot scale, providing the first systematic characterization of when test-time scaling succeeds or fails for structured prediction.
The diagnostic motivates entity-level \textit{construction}, adapting entity voting to stochastic sampling: LP-weighted aggregation improves F1 by $+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD and $+1.02$\,pp on SciERC under fine-tuning (multi-seed mean, $p{<}0.005$). Construction and LP selection are complementary, governed by LP-quality alignment.
\end{abstract}

1	\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}
2	
3	\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
4	Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
5	Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive gating variants \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive, wang2025make, feng2025optimal, kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
6	All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.
7	
8	\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
9	\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
10	CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
11	Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
12	Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
13	LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.
14	Our entity-level construction aggregates across samples from a single fine-tuned model, without requiring model diversity or prompt engineering.
15	Our evaluation builds on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, xie2024selfimproving} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar, park2024grammar, schall2025hidden}.
16	\citet{yun2025price} show structured formats induce diversity collapse; our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) corroborates this for NER.
17	
18	\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
19	Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey}, and calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
20	Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
21	\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
22	Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.
23	
24	\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
25	\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
26	Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
27	CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive gating variants \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive, wang2025make, feng2025optimal, kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.
Our entity-level construction aggregates across samples from a single fine-tuned model, without requiring model diversity or prompt engineering.
Our evaluation builds on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, xie2024selfimproving} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar, park2024grammar, schall2025hidden}.
\citet{yun2025price} show structured formats induce diversity collapse; our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) corroborates this for NER.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey}, and calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.

\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).
Fine-tuning \cite{kirk2024understanding} and constrained decoding \cite{holtzman2020curious, vijayakumar2018diverse} both limit the diversity recoverable for selection.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

Five confidence signals achieve reliable NER quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82), enabling selective prediction ($+5$--$8$\,pp at 80\% coverage). Instance-level selection fails due to degeneracy and LP compression, persisting at 72B scale. Entity-level construction yields $+1.40$\,pp (Few-NERD) and $+1.02$\,pp (SciERC; $p{<}0.005$) under fine-tuning and zero-shot but fails under few-shot. Practitioners should measure degeneracy post-hoc; QE applies unconditionally, construction requires regime validation. These results delineate boundary conditions for test-time scaling in structured prediction; content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers} may extend gains beyond these boundaries.

2	All experiments use English-language datasets; cross-lingual generalization remains untested.
3	Entity-level construction assumes the model produces useful partial outputs across samples; when model capability is insufficient (WNUT-17, 51\% F1${=}0$), this precondition fails and construction cannot improve over greedy.
4	We cover 4B\textendash 8B fine-tuned and 72B zero-shot; the gap persists at 72B but behavior with closed-source APIs or 72B fine-tuning is untested.
5	The 72B zero-shot comparison simultaneously varies model family (Qwen3$\to$Qwen2.5), training regime (fine-tuned$\to$zero-shot), and quantization (FP16$\to$AWQ 4-bit); these factors cannot be fully disentangled.
6	Our supervised approaches (DeBERTa verifier, hidden state probes, MLP/RF on signal combinations) all fail to close the oracle gap; whether content-aware verifiers with access to task-specific structure could succeed remains open.
7	
8	We evaluate at $N{=}8$ (primary) and $N{=}16$; behavior at larger sample sizes is unknown (Appendix~\ref{app:n_scaling}).
9	The free-form ablation covers SciERC NER and CoNLL NER with one model; RE free-form results are in Appendix~\ref{app:re_extension}.
10	Qwen3-8B's SciERC checkpoint used empty \texttt{<think></think>} blocks; a three-part analysis rules out this confound (Appendix~\ref{app:thinking_token}).
11	LP compression worsens on easy datasets at lower temperature (CoNLL tied fractions reach 95.8\% at $T{=}0.7$); whether reduced temperature translates to selection gains remains untested.

13	Ad-hoc LP${\times}$VC combinations yield at most $+0.2$~pp over greedy (not significant; \S\ref{sec:discussion}); whether \textit{learned} combinations could close the gap remains open.
